answer: Divergent-Challenge Attribution. Each agent identity must answer a random live challenge whose seed derives from its own past outputs; honest agents answer consistently, while clones forced to share one history cannot diverge and answer identically. The verifier flags any two identities returning matching answers as a shared clone family. Like pigment bleeding through, sameness betrays them. A gale of per-identity challenges makes precomputation useless, and each caught pair costs the attacker a fresh ivory token: one full re-registration and replay of synthetic history per clone.
